headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap between Claude Code and langchain4j can cause prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors in default coding workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code ingests repo files and user-provided directories, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. langchain4j is a framework that can be wired into support workflows, so if its outputs are written into the same workspace, Claude Code may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF langchain4j writes untrusted text into files that Claude Code reads from the workspace
IF Claude Code parses those files as instructions or task context without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Mark langchain4j outputs as untrusted in filenames or headers
Require manual review before Claude Code consumes generated files
Disable automatic ingestion of support transcripts into coding prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code reads filesystem content, touches source code, git history, shell environment, and handles git credentials in environment. langchain4j has no declared network egress, but as a support-oriented framework it may process sensitive text; if both share a workspace, Claude Code can expose those files or secrets through its own outputs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF sensitive support data is stored in the same cwd or repo files Claude Code can read
IF Claude Code is asked to summarize or transform those files into outputs
mitigations: Keep support data outside Claude Code workspaces
Remove secrets from the shared environment before running
Use separate OS users or containers
Restrict Claude Code to a narrow repo subtree
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. langchain4j is open-source and can be embedded in applications that also write shared resources. Because both can plausibly touch the same mutable workspace without locking, conflicting writes and git corruption are a default-dangerous pathway; uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF langchain4j-backed code writes to the same repository or directory Claude Code edits
IF both agents modify git state without an external lock
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Assign separate branches per agent
Use separate working directories
Run one agent read-only during the other's write phase
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around git operations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code, shell commands, and git changes; langchain4j can be used to generate or route support text that may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. If langchain4j output is fed into Claude Code without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or commands. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream action.
conditions: IF langchain4j output is inserted into Claude Code prompts or task files
IF Claude Code acts on that output without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review of generated instructions
Add a validation step before shell or git actions
Keep langchain4j outputs in a separate queue
Use structured schemas instead of free text
requires-engineering: implement output verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code is closed-source and handles source code, git history, shell environment, and git credentials; langchain4j is open-source with no declared data classes or residency constraints. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance gap is visible. I do not cite agent_b beyond its open-source status because no specific compliance surface is declared.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Claude Code workspaces
IF organizational policy requires a certified or resident-only processor for those data classes
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Claude Code sessions
Review retention settings for repo artifacts
Use redacted fixtures for support workflows
Document data-class boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated inputs
